title: Observation of nonlocal ferron-drag thermoelectricity
authors: Takuma Itoh, Takamasa Hirai, Ping Tang, Hossein Sepehri-Amin, Ryo Iguchi, Yusuke Kozuka, Takao Shimizu, Soshi Akita, Shunsuke Mori, Gerrit E. W. Bauer, Ken-ichi Uchida
abstract: The Peltier effect induces a heat current when a charge current passes through a conductor. Since a charge current is conserved at the junction between two different conductors, the difference between the heat flowing in both conductors for the same charge current leads to heating or cooling of the interface, providing an operating mechanism of solid-state heat pumps. Here, we report observation of heat absorption and release signals even in a junction-free, homogeneous metal when placed in proximity to a ferroelectric insulator. Our experiments using active thermographic imaging techniques confirm the prediction of the ferron-drag effect, i.e., the nonlocal excitation of ferrons, the collective excitation of the ferroelectric order, by conduction electrons in the adjacent metal. We reveal the electric-polarization-direction dependence of the temperature change signals and their unexpected increase with the metal thickness beyond the charge screening length, uncovering additional electron-phonon-ferron interactions in the metal/ferroelectric hybrid structure. The discovery of crosstalk between metals and ferroelectrics via remote ferrons could become both a nuisance and an opportunity for highly integrated circuits with ferroelectric barrier materials and revolutionize the design architecture of thermoelectric devices.
summary: This research reports the observation and theoretical analysis of a nonlocal thermoelectric effect called ferron-drag, occurring at the interface between metals and ferroelectric insulators. The key finding is that this heat transfer mechanism depends critically on the ferroelectric polarization and is mediated by acoustic phonons coupling electrons to electric polarization excitations (ferrons). This has implications for designing advanced thermoelectric devices.
main_problem: The study investigates observing nonlocal heat absorption/release signals (thermoelectric effect) in a homogeneous metal placed near a ferroelectric insulator, specifically quantifying the 'nonlocal ferron-drag thermoelectricity.'
main_result: They confirmed that the temperature change signal is dependent on the ferroelectric order and exhibits long-range behavior, suggesting phonon-mediated coupling between conduction electrons and electric polarization excitations (ferrons).
method: The work combines active thermographic imaging (LIT) experiments with theoretical modeling using the linearized Boltzmann equation to derive the nonlocal ferron-drag coefficient.
model_or_system: The physical system is a hybrid structure, such as Pt films on ferroelectric $	ext{LiNbO}_3$ substrates, sometimes separated by an $	ext{SiO}_2$ spacer. The theory models coupling via electron-phonon and electron-ferron interactions.
key_observables: Temperature change signals ($\Delta T$), thermoelectric signal amplitude ($A$), phase shift ($\phi$), and the nonlocal ferron-drag coefficient ($\Pi_{	ext{frr}}$).
important_parameters: Metal thickness ($t_{Pt}$), spacer barrier thickness ($t_{SiO_2}$), ferroelectric polarization direction (Z-cut vs. X-cut), and current amplitude ($J_{\omega}^{ac}$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the heat source is localized at boundaries due to nonlocal effects, and that the $	ext{SiO}_2$ spacer primarily increases distance without introducing significant additional phonon scattering.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate temperature maps showing boundary signals in ferroelectric vs. non-ferroelectric substrates; they also show dependence of signals on Pt thickness, spacer thickness, and substrate thermal conductivity ($\kappa$).
paper_structure: The paper progresses from initial experimental observation of the effect in $	ext{Pt}/	ext{LiNbO}_3$ (Chunk 1), to systematic investigation of ferroelectric vs. non-ferroelectric dependence and thickness scaling (Chunk 2), followed by theoretical modeling incorporating phonon mediation and spacer effects (Chunks 3 & 4).
why_interesting: The mechanism involves coupling between electronic excitations (conduction electrons) and collective lattice/polarization modes (ferrons) mediated by phonons, which touches upon concepts of coupled quantum oscillators and energy transport in complex solid-state systems.
analysis_basis: full PDF text, analyzed in chunks
